title: Synaptic nanostructure and dysfunction in neurodevelopmental disorders
text:
Abnormalities with synaptic proteins have been identified in multiple neurological and developmental disorders
including intellectual disability, autism spectrum disorder, and schizophrenia. Our proposed studies aim to
understand molecular and cellular mechanisms of abnormal molecular assemblies at synapses in
neurodevelopmental disorders. This research will have the potential to develop new therapeutic strategies to
modulate neuronal activity against relevant neurological disorders.

title: Functional interrogation of parasitic flatworm TRPM channels to identify novel anthelmintics
text:
Human diseases caused by parasitic flatworms afflict millions of people worldwide and cause significant
healthcare burdens in many countries. The current clinical therapy relies on a single drug (praziquantel, PZQ)
for which the parasitic target was only recently discovered – a transient receptor potential ion channel activated
by PZQ (TRPMPZQ). My proposal builds from our discovery of TRPMPZQ to develop new and improved
therapies for neglected tropical diseases caused by tapeworms (cestodes) and blood flukes (schistosomes).

title: Characterizing Alzheimer's disease molecular and anatomical imaging markers and their relationships with cognition and genetics using machine learning
text:
Project Narrative / Public Health Relevance
This proposal aims to evaluate the relationships of brain PET and MRI markers with cognition and genetics in
mild cognitive impairment/Alzheimer’s disease patients and normal controls. By leveraging complementary
information of amyloid PET, tau PET, MRI, cognitive, clinical, and genetic markers via machine learning methods,
this study will elucidate the first evidence on whether there are potential subgroups of patients relative to controls
and show their differential relationships among these markers. Upon success, this will provide a rationale for
designing larger-scale future studies and ultimately aid in precision medicine for the diagnosis and treatment of
patients with Alzheimer’s disease.

title: PROSPECT: Premalignant Oral Lesions Pathology and Epigenetic Risk Prediction Tool
text: This application responds to the PAR-22-131 RFA by validating a minimally invasive, robust, multi-stage artificial intelligence (AI)-based cytologic, histologic and epigenetic (multi-omic) biomarker to identify oral premalignant lesions (OPL) with high risk of progression to invasive oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC). Our biomarker, named the PROSPECT score, will be validated in a massive data set and a prospective study of OPL patients. There is currently no reliable clinical, histologic or molecular marker to determine individual risk in patients with the same dysplasia grade. A reliable biomarker will optimize survival in patients by optimizing risk stratification of OPLs and encouraging closer surveillance of patients with high cancer transformation risk.

title: University of Pittsburgh MWCCS Clinical Research Site
text:
The scientific leadership, operational infrastructure and research initiatives implemented by the University of
Pittsburgh MWCCS CRS will enable the MWCCS to address important questions relevant to aging and other
chronic diseases in people with and without HIV.

title: Repurposing HSP90 inhibitors as a new RTK condensate-directed therapy in cancer
text:
Gene rearrangements involving receptor tyrosine kinases (RTKs) represent an important
oncogenic driver in cancer and most of these patients are incurable with current standard of
care tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) treatment. Here we will conduct fundamental research into
how a newly discovered subcellular structure, a pathogenic biomolecular condensate formed by
the self-assembly of RTK fusion oncoproteins, is regulated by the protein chaperone network.
Our proposal will develop HSP90 inhibitors as a first-in-class, condensate-directed therapy that
targets this subcellular structure as a new and orthogonal approach to improve the survival of
cancer patients.

title: PolQ as a novel therapeutic target in AML
text:
Although tremendous progress has been made in treatment modalities of acute myeloid leukemia (AML), 
there is the necessity to improve and develop novel therapeutic approaches. Recently, we have 
identified that DNA polymerase theta (Polθ) is a key player in a novel DNA repair pathway that is 
essential for the proliferation of leukemia cells, but expendable in normal cells. 
Selective inhibitors of Polθ have been identified in our laboratories. We aim to 
develop a drug-like Polθ inhibitor that will selectively kill AML cells, while sparing 
healthy cells.

title: Defining the link between trisomy 21 and placentation defects
text:
Proper establishment of a functional placenta is integral to the short and long-term health of a person. People
with Down’s Syndrome develop abnormal placentas and are coincidentally at an increased risk for chronic
diseases that are closely associated with placental insufficiency. We hypothesize that the placenta is in part
responsible for heart defects in people living with Down’s Syndrome and aim to identify a mechanism by which
the placenta can serve as an avenue for therapeutic intervention.

title: High-Throughput Platforms to Study Synthetic Receptors, Natural Molecules, and New Pathway Inhibitors
text:
Advances in computational and experimental protein engineering have ushered in a new era of biomolecule
development with both fundamental and applied aims, but current approaches lack the ability to develop and
study synthetic receptors and inhibitory molecules in high throughput. We propose to develop protein
engineering platforms for robust inhibitor development, for studying synthetic receptors, and for a combined
computational and experimental pipeline to engineer and study natural molecules. Once developed, these
platforms will be applied to study fundamental questions in cell signaling, in development of disease pathologies,
and in biomolecular sequence-function and structure-function relationships.

title: Targeting Oligosaccharyltransferse Redundancy for the Treatment of Osteosarcoma
text:
A major challenge for advancing cancer therapies from bioactive small molecules to lead candidates is the ability
to address pharmacokinetic liabilities that prevent translation. We have identified small molecules that target the
oligosaccharyltransferase (OST) as a new class of therapeutics for oncology. The proposed research will use
medicinal chemistry to optimize OST inhibitors, elucidate their cellular mechanisms of action, and advance this
strategy to preclinical testing in xenograft and PDX models of osteosarcoma.

title: USC Geroscience Training in the Biology of Aging
text:
America’s aging society requires solutions for the debilitating chronic diseases that diminish health and quality
of life at older ages and that also threaten to overwhelm the capacity of the medical establishment and the
national wealth. Ultimately, if we want to increase health across all ages, we need to understand what happens
during natural aging and also in the context of age-related diseases like Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s
disease, coronary artery disease, diabetes and metabolic diseases, late onset cancers, rheumatoid and arthritic
diseases, stroke, respiratory diseases, and susceptibility to infectious agents. This Geroscience training program
in the Biology of Aging prepares researchers with the tools to discover the mechanistic complexities and
underlying causes of aging and age-related diseases, and to design rational preventative measures for clinical
testing.

title: Leveraging Single Cell Stimulation to Untangle Parallel Perceptual Pathways in the Human Retina
text:
Characterization of human retinal ganglion cells in action will add to our understanding of the organization of
visual perception and of the neural code leaving the eye. This work could inform the development of human
visual prostheses. It could also be used to develop diagnostic tools to better inform the treatment of glaucoma,
by detecting abnormalities in OFF retinal ganglion cell receptive fields.

title: Regulatory Strategies for the Control of Activity-Dependent Gene Expression in a Single Neuron Type
text:
Neuronal gene expression profiles reflect cellular activity histories. Distinct activity patterns are transduced into
specific gene expression programs which encode the properties of the inciting pattern. Here we exploit the
simple, precisely controllable, and easily accessible C. elegans nervous system to describe the molecular
pathways which orchestrate activity-dependent gene expression via genetic and epigenetic mechanisms.

title: Epigenetic regulation in cardiac development
text:
This project is tightly aligned with the NIH mission by unveiling new epigenetic mechanisms that account for
the embryonic heart development, with a focus on the DNA methylation homeostasis and maternal metabolic
influence. Our studies will furnish important insights that are immediately relevant to the precise temporal and
spatial epigenetic regulation which contributes to the normal heart development. Our discoveries will
significantly promote healthy cardiac development and illuminate previously underappreciated epigenetic
mechanisms underpinning congenital cardiovascular diseases and cardiovascular diseases.

title: Novel approaches to improve comprehensive profiling of the epigenome and epitranscriptome
text:
Comprehensive profiling of DNA and RNA molecules, including nucleotide modifications, is important for a
complete understanding of how genes are normally regulated or dysregulated in disease. To this end, we are
developing approaches using long-read sequencing technology to simultaneously detect in vivo genome-wide
DNA modification and DNA accessibility and correlate changes with complete RNA sequences, along with
RNA modifications. We will apply our approaches to uncover how epigenome regulation affects
epitranscriptome regulation by suppressing expression of key epigenome modulators.

title: Determining network signatures of pharmacoresistance in focal cortical dysplasia-related epilepsy
text:
Focal cortical dysplasia (FCD) is the most common cause of surgically-remediable, pharmacoresistant
epilepsy in children, yet based on current imaging and clinical characteristics it is not possible to predict which
children will develop pharmacoresistance, and which patients may have a more benign course of drug-
responsive epilepsy. There is evidence that FCD epileptic activity can impact and alter distributed cortical
functional networks, and this study uses functional imaging techniques to define network alterations as a
marker of pharmacoresistance. The results of this proposal will allow clinicians to identify earlier those FCD
patients who will benefit from surgical resection, sparing them the years of burden of ongoing seizures and
cognitive, developmental and economic impact of chronic antiseizure medication therapy.

title: Unlocking the Therapeutic Potential of the Veratrum Alkaloids
text:
Neurotoxic natural products that inhibit the signaling of voltage-gated ion channels have
garnered considerable attention from the pharmaceutical industry as non-opioid analgesics. One class of
neurotoxic alkaloids that are still fairly unexplored are those found in the flowering plants of the genus Veratrum,
due in part to their structural diversity and synthetic complexity. The Trauner group has recently completed a
total synthesis of the Veratrum alkaloids veratramine and 20-epi-veratramine that can be utilized to access
several other naturally occurring Veratrum alkaloids and to thoroughly evaluate the therapeutic potential of this
class of molecule.

title: Novel therapeutic approaches to treatment of botulinum neurotoxin poisoning
text:
This project aims to develop novel botulism therapeutics based on the use of natural neuronal receptors
and trafficking patterns normally employed by the targeted toxin itself. Unlike available antibody-based
therapeutics and small molecule inhibitors of the light chain metalloprotease, botulism therapeutics based on
atoxic derivatives of botulinum neurotoxin (BoNT) can reach an intracellular target in a post‐exposure setting. In
addition, unlike conventional, small molecule therapeutics which would equally affect all cells in the body with
potentially deleterious cytotoxic side effects, the proposed atoxic BoNT-based molecular vehicle will specifically
deliver a therapeutic moiety only to the cytosol of the target cells (motor neurons). This is a unique and innovative
approach toward treating not only botulism, as embodied in this proposal, but also toward treating numerous
infectious and neurodegenerative diseases in which therapeutic targets reside and exert their action
intracellularly.

title: Continuing Education for Structural Biology Mentors
text: Cryo-EM data processing for structural biology improves and accelerates drug discovery that treats diseases and is driving innovation and economic growth in the pharmaceutical industry. Our proposed continuing education program aims to develop a portable solution with integrated data, software, workflow, and a sustainable computing environment that trains structural biology investigators to strengthen their Cryo-EM data processing skills, as well as provides them with a training solution that can be adapted and used in continuing education programs in Cryo-EM data processing at their home institution or local community. This enhanced research training program will have the potential to provide and scale sustainable continuing education in Cryo-EM data processing to investigators and students pursuing biomedical careers of the future.

title: Discovery and engineering of CRISPR/Cas systems
text:
CRISPR/Cas systems are exponentially growing as gene and RNA editing and detection technologies with a
huge potential for applications in diagnosis and treatment of a range of genetic diseases. The proposed research
will lead to the discovery, understanding, and engineering CRISPR/Cas systems to solve challenging issues of
lower efficiency, poor specificity, and lack of control. A deeper understanding and development of next
generation of CRISPR/Cas technologies for diagnosis and treatment of diseases would have a transformative
impact to a wider research community across multiple disciplines, institutes and centers of the NIH.
